data.title: Ireland extends visa waiver for Indians until December 2026: How to qualify
data.description:
Want to visit Ireland this winter? Travellers from India can do so without applying for a separate Irish visa if they meet the eligibility conditions under the country's Short-Stay Visa Waiver Programme, which has been extended until December 31, 2026.
 
The extension was announced on the official portal of Ireland's Department of Justice, Home Affairs and Migration. The programme, which was originally due to expire on October 31, 2026, has been extended by two months, keeping the facility available through the Christmas and New Year holiday season.
 
Under the scheme, eligible travellers holding a qualifying UK short-stay visitor or business visa can also visit the Republic of Ireland without submitting a separate Irish visa application. An Irish short-stay visa normally costs €60 for a single entry and €100 for multiple entries, excluding visa application centre service charges.
  
First introduced in July 2011 to encourage tourism and business travel from emerging markets, the programme has been extended several times. The latest extension offers some relief to Indian travellers planning winter holidays. This is particularly relevant because Ireland removed the right to appeal short-stay visa refusals from June 1, 2026, requiring rejected applicants to submit fresh applications instead.
 

How does Ireland's visa waiver programme work?

 
Holding a valid UK visa alone does not make a traveller eligible for the waiver. Applicants must meet specific entry and stay conditions, according to Ireland's Immigration Service Delivery.
 
Enter the UK first: Travellers must first enter the United Kingdom using their qualifying UK visa and clear immigration control before proceeding to Ireland. Those flying directly from India or another third country to Dublin cannot use the waiver. An exception applies to travellers who have already used a multiple-entry UK visa to enter the UK on an earlier trip and still have valid permission to stay.
 
Stay for up to 90 days: Visitors can remain in Ireland for a maximum of 90 days or until their UK permission to stay expires, whichever comes first.
 
The arrangement is not reciprocal: The waiver allows eligible UK visa holders to visit Ireland, but an Irish short-stay visa does not permit entry into the UK, including Northern Ireland. Travellers entering Northern Ireland and then crossing into the Republic of Ireland will need a double-entry or multiple-entry UK visa if they intend to return to Northern Ireland.
 
Border checks still apply: Irish immigration officers retain the authority to question travellers and refuse entry. Visitors should carry their passport containing the used UK visa, evidence of their entry into the UK, return tickets, accommodation bookings and proof of sufficient funds.
 

Which countries are eligible for Ireland's visa waiver?

 
The programme covers nationals of 21 countries, including India. The complete list is:
 
India, China (excluding Hong Kong and Macau), Indonesia, Kazakhstan, the Philippines, Thailand, Uzbekistan, Vietnam, Bahrain, Kuwait, Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Kosovo, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Serbia, Turkey, Colombia and Peru.
 
However, not every category of UK visa qualifies for the facility.
 
Eligible UK visas:
 
Standard short-stay visitor visas.
Short-stay business visas granted for stays of up to 180 days.
 
UK permissions not covered:
 
Electronic Travel Authorisations (ETAs).
Transit visas.
Marriage and civil partnership visitor visas.
Long-term visas, including student, work and family reunification permissions exceeding 180 days.
 
There is also an important distinction for nationals of the 21 eligible countries who live in the UK on long-term visas. They cannot use the waiver and must apply separately for an Irish visa. However, they are exempt from the Irish visa application fee.
 

How does Ireland's visa appeal rule affect Indian travellers?

 
The visa waiver extension comes at a time when Indian travellers face tighter procedures for challenging Irish visa refusals.
 
From June 1, 2026, Ireland removed the right to appeal refusals of short-stay (Type C) visas. The change applies to applicants of all nationalities, including Indians applying for tourist, business or family-visit visas. Limited exceptions apply to cases covered by the EU Free Movement Directive.
 
Under the revised rules, applicants whose short-stay visa applications are rejected on or after June 1 cannot challenge the decision through the earlier appeal process. They must submit fresh applications, addressing the reasons for the previous rejection.
 
The change applies to short-stay visas and does not mean that Indian travellers are barred from applying for an Irish visa. It also does not affect their eligibility for the Short-Stay Visa Waiver Programme, provided they meet its conditions.
 

Will Ireland extend the visa waiver programme beyond 2026?

 
Irish immigration authorities have not yet confirmed whether the programme will continue beyond December 31, 2026.
 
Travellers planning trips that extend beyond this date should check the Immigration Service Delivery portal for further announcements or apply for a separate Irish visa well in advance.
 
Separately, Indian and Chinese nationals are also covered by the British-Irish Visa Scheme (BIVS), a distinct arrangement that allows eligible travellers to visit both the UK and Ireland using a single visa endorsed under the scheme.

data.title: No formal bilateral talks between India, Pak on sidelines of SCO forum
data.description:
There were "no formal bilateral talks" held between India and Pakistan on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Civilisational Dialogue Forum, Union Culture Secretary Vivek Aggarwal said on Sunday.

Pakistan's Federal Minister Musadik Masood Malik attended the three-day forum here hosted by India at the historic Purana Quila.

Malik later in the evening, interacting with the media, said, "When you will call me for talk on Indus (Water Treaty), that time, we will surely talk on Indus (treaty). This time, you have not called me here for (talks on) the Indus treaty; this time you have called me to talk...," Malik said.

 

"You have called me this time to talk about the issue in the context of the SCO forum, the regional issues, its relationship with culture, for which I am here," he told reporters here.

The forum was hosted by the Ministry of Culture and the Ministry of External Affairs.

Earlier, at a press interaction held at the venue, shortly before the closure of the forum asked if any formal bilateral talks were held between India and Pakistan on the sidelines; Aggarwal said, "There were no formal bilateral talks between the two sides." However, he said that members of the Indian side did have interactions with him over banquets and during the conference, as well as there were other "informal discussions" with him during the course of the forum, as with other ministers too.

"In general, there were also meetings between ministers and heads of delegations, as the aim of this (multilateral) forum is to exchange views, so there were many meetings, and a lot of things were discussed," the culture secretary said.

However, he didn't specify how many bilateral talks took place during the course of the Forum hosted by India from November 20-22.

Asked if any bilateral meeting took place with Iran, he said, "There was a bilateral meeting with Iran. And India is in constant touch with Iran, and on areas in which there can be any cultural exchange, we are always in discussion. And discussions took place during the Summit too." The secretary said that during the bilateral meeting, "ideas have been thrown, though no such project has been concretised yet. But the discussions and engagements are on".

The Iranian Embassy in India, in a post on X on Sunday, said that, at the civilisational summit, Tehran proposed setting up an "SCO Joint Network for Written Heritage and Civilisational Memory".

Dr Faridoddin Faridasr, Cultural Counsellor of the Islamic Republic of Iran in India, addressed the First SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum in New Delhi, highlighting the importance of shared civilisational heritage as a foundation for cultural cooperation and mutual understanding among SCO member states, it said.

In his remarks, he emphasised the historical role of the "Persian language as a language of science, literature, administration and cultural exchange across Central Asia, the Indian subcontinent and neighbouring regions, describing it as an important part of the shared cultural and historical heritage of the region".

Referring to Iran's successful cultural cooperation with India, he highlighted the activities of the Noor International Microfilm Centre, affiliated with the Embassy of the Islamic Republic of Iran in New Delhi. Since 1990, the Centre has collaborated with 72 academic and cultural institutions in India, resulting in the digitisation of "more than 150,000 Persian and Arabic manuscripts," the restoration and preservation of over three million pages of historical documents, and the preparation of nearly 300 catalogues, the embassy said.

Faridasr also referred to the ongoing joint projects with cultural institutions in Telangana and Hyderabad for the digitisation, restoration and preservation of historical Persian documents and manuscripts.

As a practical initiative to strengthen regional cultural cooperation, he proposed the establishment of an "SCO Joint Network for Written Heritage and Civilizational Memory." "The proposed network would focus on the preservation and digitisation of manuscripts and historical documents, the exchange of technical expertise and training in manuscript restoration, and the promotion of shared linguistic and literary heritage through joint research, publications and exhibitions," the embassy said in a detailed post on X.

He reaffirmed Iran's "readiness to share its experience and technical expertise with other SCO member states", stressing that the preservation of shared civilisational heritage provides an important opportunity to strengthen mutual trust, cultural understanding and cooperation across the region.

The forum was inaugurated by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on November 20. It saw the participation of delegates from various Shanghai Cooperation Organisation member countries, including Pakistan and other countries.

data.title: Auto retail hits record 5.525 mn units during 42-day festive season: Fada
data.description:
Automobile retail sales in India rose 2.21 per cent year-on-year to a record 5.525 million units during the 42-day festive season this year, despite a high base following the GST 2.0-led demand surge last year, dealer body Fada said on Monday.

According to the Federation of Automobile Dealers Associations (Fada), total vehicle retail sales stood at 55,25,490 units during the 42-day festive period of 2026, the highest-ever for the corresponding period.

Compared with the festive season of 2024, vehicle retail sales registered a growth of 23.95 per cent, indicating sustained demand momentum following the GST rate rationalisation.

Two-wheeler retail sales grew 3.67 per cent to 43,13,276 units, while three-wheeler sales rose 5.32 per cent to 193,576 units.

 

Commercial vehicle retail sales increased 7.13 per cent to 155,761 units, tractor sales grew 2.24 per cent to 103,809 units and construction equipment sales surged 26.06 per cent to 10,452 units.

However, passenger vehicle retail sales declined 7.16 per cent to 748,616 units against 806,322 units in the year-ago period.

The biggest highlight of the season was the surge in electric vehicle adoption, with EV retail sales jumping 52.62 per cent to cross five hundred thousand units for the first time during a single festive period, led by electric two-wheelers (61.10 pc rise) and electric passenger vehicles (up 72.91 pc), with electric commercial vehicles more than doubling.

Close to one in ten festive vehicles sold this season was electric, Fada stated.

Fada President Sai Giridhar said: "The 42-day festive season of 2026 will be remembered as the year Indian auto retail set a record on top of a record. Against last year's extraordinary base, which got amplified by GST 2.0, the twin festivals delivered an all-time high -- festive retails this year still grew 2.21 per cent to 55,25,490 units, the highest-ever 42-day festive season in our history." Looking ahead, Fada said India was approaching a historic milestone of recording over 3 crore vehicle retail sales in a calendar year for the first time.

The festive season has set the stage for this achievement, it added.

data.title: Maruti Suzuki gains 2% on price hike; stock up 14% in one week
data.description:
Maruti Suzuki India share price movement

 
Share price of Maruti Suzuki India hit a four-month high of ₹14,338.25, gaining 2 per cent on the BSE in Monday’s intraday deals in an otherwise weak market after the company hiked prices of select vehicle models effective November 22, 2026. In comparison, the BSE Sensex was down 0.8 per cent at 83,261 at 10:20 AM.
 
In the past week, the stock price of Maruti Suzuki India outperformed the market by soaring 14 per cent, compared to a 1 per cent rise in the BSE Sensex. Further, in the past month, the market price of the passenger vehicles (PV) company rallied 27 per cent, against a 14 per cent surge in the benchmark index. Currently, Maruti Suzuki India quotes at its highest level since July 2026.
 
 

Maruti Suzuki India hikes price of select models

 
In a press release, Maruti Suzuki India said it increased the prices of select vehicle models effective November 22, 2026, due to sustained cost pressures. The company stated that rising input costs made it necessary to pass on a part of the additional expenses to customers while trying to minimise the impact. The estimated volume-weighted average price increase is around 0.31 per cent.
 
The price hike reflects the growing cost pressures faced by the automobile industry. Given the recent correction around commodity prices, consecutive price hikes can provide operating leverage and support margin expansion from the March 2027 quarter (Q4FY27) onwards, ICICI Securities said in a note. 
ALSO READ: Stock Market LIVE: Sensex at day's low, down 700 pts, Nifty below 25,600; Nifty Defence drops 1%
 

Brokerages view on Maruti Suzuki India, Auto sector

 
The automobile sector delivered a strong performance in the July to September 2026 (Q2FY27) quarter, supported by GST-led affordability, healthy festive demand, premiumization, and improving consumer sentiment.
 
While a favourable base and GST-led purchase deferrals in the previous year supported growth, management commentary remains constructive, with PV and two-wheelers (2W) original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) expecting high single-digit domestic growth in the second half (October to March) of the financial year 2026-27 (H2FY27E). Analysts at Choice Institutional Equities believe this shall be supported by sustained demand momentum and favourable consumer sentiment across key vehicle segments over the next few quarters.
 
Meanwhile, commodity inflation is showing initial signs of easing, with aluminium, copper and steel rebar prices declining 9.3 per cent, 8.5 per cent and 1.9 per cent, respectively, during October/November compared to Q2FY27. Elevated commodity prices in H1FY27 significantly pressured profitability across the auto value chain, with Maruti Suzuki’s raw material expense increasing 510 bps YoY in Q1FY27 and Q2FY27. The moderation in input costs, particularly aluminium and copper, should benefit OEMs and Ancillaries, the brokerage firm said. Further, it expects lower input costs, calibrated price hikes and operating leverage to support gradual margin recovery from Q4FY27E, with greater benefits potentially flowing through in FY28E.
 
Meanwhile, Maruti Suzuki’s management expects margins to improve over Q2–Q3, supported by easing commodity prices, normalization of settlement cycles and the benefit of vehicle price hikes implemented in June (0.5 per cent) and August. Management remains optimistic on FY27 growth, expecting around 10 per cent volume growth, supported by demand recovery, new product launches, capacity expansion and improving exports, while near-term growth remains constrained by production ramp-up.
 
Over the longer term, Maruti remains well-positioned through investments across ICE, CNG (40 per cent portfolio), Hybrid, Hydrogen and electric vehicles (EVs), with the ₹3,900  crore EV-focused line at Hansalpur and upcoming EV launches supporting sustainable growth, analysts at Axis Securities said with a ‘Buy’ rating on the stock and target price of ₹15,920 per share. Disclaimer: Views and outlook in this report belong to the brokerages and analysts cited. They do not reflect the views of Business Standard. Readers are advised to exercise discretion.

data.title: Nepal PM Balen Shah meets PM Modi in Delhi: What's on the agenda?
data.description:
Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah received a ceremonial welcome at Rashtrapati Bhavan in New Delhi on Monday, with Prime Minister Narendra Modi in attendance, as he began the second day of his two-day state visit to India.
 
Shah is scheduled to hold delegation-level talks with PM Modi on Monday. During these talks, the two leaders will review the full range of India-Nepal relations and exchange views on regional and international issues of mutual interest, according to the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA).
 
Following the bilateral talks, the two leaders will jointly address a press conference. PM Modi will host an official luncheon in honour of the Nepali prime minister and his delegation on the same day.
 
 
Shah arrived in India on Sunday for a two-day state visit from November 22 to 23 at PM Modi's invitation. This is his first visit to India since taking office in March 2026 and his first bilateral visit abroad as Nepal's prime minister.
 

Nepal's PM Balen Shah in India: What's on the agenda?

 
Energy cooperation, infrastructure development, trade and connectivity are expected to be among the key issues during the talks between PM Modi and Shah.
 
The two countries are looking to strengthen cooperation in hydropower, railways, road and air connectivity, investment and infrastructure. They are also expected to discuss ways to expand economic ties and address pending issues in the bilateral relationship.
 
India and Nepal are also discussing a development package worth $2 billion. If finalised, part of the package could go towards reconstruction work in Nepal following the glacial floods in August, which damaged homes and hydropower projects.
 
The two sides are also expected to sign agreements covering investments in Nepal's education, healthcare and hydropower sectors. Other areas of cooperation could include improving connectivity and reciprocal overflight access.
 
An integrated check post at Banbasa in Uttarakhand is also among the infrastructure projects planned during the visit.
 
A 52-member business delegation is accompanying the Nepalese prime minister. A Nepal-India Business Forum is also scheduled to meet during the visit, providing an opportunity to discuss trade and investment opportunities between the two countries.
 

PM Modi, Balen Shah to flag off Saryu-Kamala Express

 
Improving cross-border rail connectivity is another key part of the visit. PM Modi and Shah will virtually flag off the Saryu-Kamala Express on Monday, a new weekly train service connecting Ayodhya Cantt in Uttar Pradesh with Janakpur Dham in Nepal.
 
The service is expected to improve travel between two important religious destinations associated with the Ramayana tradition. Janakpur Dham is revered as the birthplace of Goddess Sita, while Ayodhya is associated with the birthplace of Lord Ram.
 
The train will have stoppages at Gorakhpur, Basti, Raxaul, Sitamarhi, Madhubani and Jaynagar, improving rail access for passengers in several districts of Uttar Pradesh and Bihar.
 
The Saryu-Kamala Express is part of wider efforts by the two countries to improve railway connectivity. Other projects include the Jaynagar-Bijalpura-Bardibas and Jogbani-Biratnagar rail links. The proposed Raxaul-Kathmandu railway line is also expected to strengthen transport links between the two neighbours.
 

Jaishankar meets Nepal PM Balen Shah

 
Before his meeting with PM Modi, Shah met External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar in New Delhi on Sunday.
 
Following the meeting, Jaishankar said India cherishes its special friendship with Nepal and looked forward to the Nepalese prime minister's engagements with PM Modi. The two sides discussed key areas of bilateral cooperation, including connectivity, trade, transit, energy, culture, education and people-to-people ties.
 
(With agency inputs)

data.title: Tata Steel divests tubes biz: Will it unlock value? What analysts say
data.description:
Tata Steel share price: Tata group company Tata Steel has announced a strategic divestment plan, which will help unlock value for the steel major, analysts believe. 
 
While Tata Steel shares slumped almost 6 per cent following the deal announcement on Monday, brokerages largely retained their bullish views on the counter, with both Emkay and JM Financial assigning 'BUY' calls. On Monday, Tata Steel stock was down 6.04 per cent at ₹167.
 
As part of the agreement, Tata Steel has approved divestment of its tubes business and its entire equity stake in Tata Steel Colors (formerly Tata BlueScope Steel) to APL Apollo for aggregate consideration of up to ₹28000 crore (equivalent to approximately ₹22/share). 
 
 
The Tubes Business will be transferred for cash consideration of up to ₹11700 crore, while the entire 100 per cent stake in Tata Steel Colors will be sold for ₹16300 crore in cash. Both transactions are inter-conditional and are expected to close
simultaneously, subject to regulatory approvals and customary conditions, by March 31, 2028. ALSO READ: APL Apollo tanks 15% on Tata Steel deal: Why analysts see near-term pain
 
Furthermore, earlier on Monday, the company said it will also pick a majority stake in the company by acquiring the entire promoter stake of 26.6 per cent in APL Apollo, an MOU with SG Tech Engineering Private Ltd, a company associated with the Promoter Group of APL Apollo, to set up exclusive contract manufacturing facilities of 5 MTPA of Colour Coated products.
 

What analysts say on Tata Steel

Analysts believe the deal announced could lead to significant value unlocking of through sale of downstream business, but also marks a pivot away from the earlier planned expansion of tubes capacity, along with doubling the Colors business.
 
"We view the transactions positively as a significant value-unlocking exercise and an important step towards downstream portfolio rationalisation," said JM Financial analysts. 
 
The aggregate consideration of up to ₹28000 crore provides substantial cash realisation and financial flexibility, equivalent to approximately 31 per cent of Tata Steel’s September 2026 consolidated net debt of ₹91423 crore. 
 
The monetisation, said JM Financial, allows Tata Steel to unlock capital from downstream businesses and potentially redeploy it towards core steelmaking operations, capacity expansion and balance-sheet strengthening.  ALSO READ: Tata Steel to acquire 26.6% stake in APL Apollo for ₹15,510 crore
 
Meanwhile, Emkay Global said that while it views the transaction as a significant strategic reset for Tata Steel, it is unsure if is an unambiguously positive portfolio-rationalization exercise. 
 
The consideration offers meaningful capital unlocking (~80 per cent of FY26 EBITDA and 31 per cent of 2Q net debt-to-EBITDA), but the divestment of businesses generating ₹16100 crore in revenue, along with combined net worth of Rs43bn, needs to be assessed against the earnings and growth potential being relinquished. 
 
Loss of downstream conversion economics and strategic optionality also warrants attention, especially without a disclosed long-term supply arrangement with APL Apollo, it noted. Emkay has a 'BUY' rating and a target price of ₹210 on the stock.
 
JM also noted the loss of earnings from the divested businesses, but added that transactions could improve capital efficiency, sharpen strategic focus and strengthen Tata Steel’s financial flexibility," it added. This brokerage has a 'BUY' call with a target of ₹240. 
Disclaimer: Views and outlook in this report belong to the brokerages and analysts cited. They do not reflect the views of Business Standard. Readers are advised to exercise discretion.

data.title: 'Remain constructive on Indian equities irrespective of how global markets do'
data.description:
Indian markets have outperformed global peers in the last few weeks as foreign money chased stocks back home. Sandeep Tandon, founder & chief investment officer, quant Group, told Puneet Wadhwa in an in-person interview on the sidelines of SIF360 Summit in New Delhi that the fall in artificial intelligence (AI)-related stocks is a relatively minor correction within a larger global structural bull run in AI-related stocks globally. Edited excerpts:
 
What do you see as the biggest inflection point for Indian equities in 2027?
 
The global equity market, particularly the AI-led investment theme, has gone through a downturn. This creates a great opportunity for India, both on an absolute and relative basis. Moreover, India's macroeconomic picture is improving. Whether it is crude oil, the currency or corporate earnings, the overall environment is looking favourable. I am therefore more constructive on Indian equities, irrespective of how global markets perform.
 
 
Foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) have returned to Indian markets. Is this partly driven by expectations of changes in the long-term and short-term capital gains tax structure, or is it reallocation of capital due to a sell-off in AI-related stocks globally?
 
FPIs have returned because they are opportunistic investors. They had left India because they were finding better opportunities elsewhere in the world. Now they are coming back.
 
Investors should not look at returns in absolute terms alone; they should look at relative opportunities. FPIs have been affected significantly by developments in global markets and are now returning to India. That is also why there is an urgency to deploy capital by December.
 
They already had exposure to India, which explains some of this urgency. So, I would not attribute their return to expectations of changes in LTCG or STCG taxation. They are opportunists. We should deal with them as such. Investors look for opportunities and capitalise on them.
 
Do you think this opportunity will sustain for Indian equities over the next six months to a year?
 
It is difficult to say what will happen over the next three or six years. The next one or two quarters look encouraging. We will have to see how the numbers shape up and what develops.
 
Do you think the AI theme has run its course, or is this a correction within a larger structural trend?
 
It is a correction. AI represents a major transformational phase in our lives. It is comparable to the changes we saw in 2017-18, when the world underwent a significant transformation. So, this is a relatively minor correction within a larger global structural bull run in AI-related stocks globally.
 
How should mutual fund investors allocate money?
 
Given the volatile global environment, long-short products are among the best options. One can have a one-year, three-year or five-year view, and the structural outlook for India may be positive. But nobody can predict with certainty what will happen over three years. We will play the opportunities as they emerge.
  
Which sectors do you expect investors to favour in 2027?
 
Real assets, particularly Indian hard assets. Ports, airports, power and utilities are among the areas I would focus on.
 
Does this mean infrastructure will be a major investment theme in 2027? What would you advise those who have missed the recent market rally?
 
They should invest in quantitative equity long-short products. Any time is a good time to invest in these products because they can capitalise on opportunities on both sides of the market.
 
How should investors invetsors allocate between SIFs, and other investment products in the mutual fund segment?
 
A 50:50 allocation. If one already has investments in mutual funds, your incremental allocation should be split equally. Over the next five years, investors should aim to balance their portfolios with 50 per cent in SIPs and 50 per cent in these products. This is also why we believe such products could account for 50 per cent of the active mutual fund industry's assets in the next 10 years.
 
Rising inflation and its potential impact on corporate earnings are another concern for investors. Are corporate earnings factoring in this possibility?
 
We are in a structural bull run in interest rates globally, although the impact is likely to be less pronounced in India. So, the global problem is relatively less of a concern for India. But we have to learn to live with it.
 
Inflation in the US used to be around 5-6 per cent earlier. Just because it has now turned negative by a percentage point does not mean that becomes the benchmark. I do not see this as a major problem. There will be some pain over the long term, but we have to live with it. How long can we keep worrying about it? There are opportunities somewhere, and money will flow towards them.
 
What is your big message to investors for 2027?
 
SIP-type products are a great investment option from a risk-adjusted return perspective. Investors need to understand the importance of risk-adjusted returns rather than focusing only on absolute or relative returns. The focus on risk-adjusted numbers is what I believe will change the way people look at SIPs.
 
What kind of returns should Indian investors expect from equities over the next 12-18 months?
 
That is a difficult question to answer. Investors should put their money into the right products. These products can generate returns and outperform their benchmarks. They should not focus on absolute return numbers.

data.title: Gold, Copper, Zinc, Aluminium: Morgan Stanley's outlook on key metals
data.description:
Prices of metals such as copper, zinc, aluminium, gold and silver have been on a downtrend since the last few trading sessions in India and globally, as concerns regarding rising inflation higher yields, possibility of 'higher for longer' interest rates in the United States (US) and a pullback in artificial intelligence (AI)- related spending cast a shadow.
 
The Nifty Metal index slid over 2 per cent in trade on Monday, with stocks such as Tata Steel, Hindustan Copper, Sail, NMDC, National Aluminium slipping up to 5.5 per cent in intraday deals. APL Apollo Tubes, though news-driven, was the top loser that skidded over 13 per cent in intraday deals. 
ALSO READ: APL Apollo tanks 14%, Tata Steel 5% on ₹28K-cr deal: What it means for cos
 
 
Rate cuts through 2024/2025, the AI theme and focus on strategic minerals had boosted investor engagement in metals, according to analysts at Morgan Stanley, with positioning back at 2021/22 levels. With interest rates rising again though, metals are struggling as a non-yielding asset with exposure to rate-sensitive construction and autos markets.
 
The weakness in the AI theme is not helping, particularly for copper, Morgan Stanley said in a November 18 report, which had held up relative to other AI-exposed assets, while a stronger US dollar (USD) also hurts.
 
Here's how Morgan Stanley sees prices of metals play out in the next few months.
 
Gold: Gold's long-term drivers remain intact. Physical demand is holding up well, with China's PBOC adding 26 tonnes in October and central bank buying on track to surpass 2025 levels, while exchange traded funds (ETFs) seeing very modest gold sales so far despite falling prices. This suggests support for real assets driven by concerns over government debt and fiscal sustainability. 
 
If oil prices move lower more decisively and/or the market gets to the point where it believes the US Fed has finished hiking, gold prices could move higher, while a stagflation scenario with softer growth and more stubborn inflation could also be supportive. Timing remains challenging though, and the systematic positioning moves and sensitivity to technical levels could keep gold volatility high in the short-term. 
ALSO READ: Copper falls to near five-month low as firm dollar, AI concerns weigh
 
Copper: The cautious view on copper by end-2027 has played out quicker-than-expected with a combination of factors driving the weakness. Negative macro pressure from rising interest rates and stronger USD was already building for commodities as a whole, while the broad-based AI selloff has brought additional weakness.
 
Copper has seen a strong correlation with the "Mag7" stocks this year, implying some of its elevated positioning was related to the AI build-out. Our thesis of copper deficit into next year remains unchanged, and we would remain buyers if there is an overshoot (MSe $13,675/t for LME 2027 average, $12,800/t (Q4 2027).
 
With the need for more projects to be developed to avoid large future deficits, copper is expected to broadly stay above incentive price (MSe $10,700/t real 2026$, $12,400/t nominal 2033), but it's difficult to call exactly when dip buying will emerge, and we can of course have volatility around that level with changes in AI sentiment and US tariff policy.  
 
 
Aluminium: Aluminium already broke through its moving averages in September, but had held above $3000/t until recently with the market still quite tight for now despite an expected 2027 surplus. Our expectations for the 2027 surplus haven't changed, driven new capacity in Indonesia and Angola, a recovery in West Asia and small smelter restarts in Europe and the US. Aluminium demand can also be particularly sensitive to an economic slowdown in the face of rising interest rates, while positioning on LME remains higher than the rest of the complex, implying potential for additional downside.
 
Zinc: from a fundamental perspective, we see a strong set up for zinc with a very tight supply side. Mine supply is expected to contract 1.8% in 2026 to 12.7 Mt, lower than output in 2015, while recovery next year is likely 2H weighted, leaving scope for further near-term tightness.  
ALSO READ: Chris Wood hikes exposure to Indian equities as AI trade falters
 
Meanwhile, ex-China remains reliant on Chinese exports to balance the market which face risks from domestic smelter struggles and falling SHFE inventories. However, demand has been weak, with less than 1% growth expected this year globally, while higher interest rates bring additional downside risk. LME zinc positioning looks unusual versus other metals, with both long and short positioning rising sharply,
highlighting diverging market views which could keep prices volatile.
 
Nickel: The market remains very focused on Indonesia's mining policy, particularly the upcoming release of RKAB (mining) quotas for 2027, which may remain restrictive. Some operators have also floated potential production cuts due to margin pressures with elevated energy and sulphur prices.
 
Disclaimer: Views and outlook in this report belong to the brokerages and analysts cited. They do not reflect the views of Business Standard. Readers are advised to exercise discretion.

data.title: Multibagger stock: SG Mart surges 13% to record high on fundraise buzz
data.description:
SG Mart share price today: Shares of SG Mart extended their winning streak for a second consecutive session on Monday, hitting an all-time high despite weakness in the market. The stock opened 4.5 per cent higher at ₹1,150 and extended its gains to hit an intraday high of ₹1,238.70, rising 13 per cent.
 
The buying interest in the stock was supported by an announcement that the company may consider a fund-raising proposal.
 
As of 9:50 AM, SG Mart shares were trading 12.3 per cent higher at ₹1,231, retaining most of their intraday gains.
 
The stock was among the most actively traded equities by value. According to exchange data, around two million shares changed hands, with a total turnover of ₹233.35 crore.
 
 
With Monday's rally, the stock has gained 21 per cent over two consecutive trading sessions.

data.title: L&T bags large order worth ₹5,000 crore to deploy AI cluster in Chennai
data.description:
Larsen & Toubro (L&T) on Monday said its group company Vyoma.AI, through its artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure subsidiary LTN Compute, has secured a multi-year engagement to deploy additional NVIDIA B300 graphics processing units (GPUs) at its Chennai data centre. The order, classified as “Large” by L&T, is worth up to ₹5,000 crore.
 
The additional GPUs will power an inference infrastructure provider's AI-native platform as part of a 10,000-GPU cluster, the company said in an exchange filing.
 
“The infrastructure will power the inference infrastructure provider’s AI-native platform, enabling it to train, fine-tune and deploy specialised AI models for high-performance inference at commercial scale,” L&T said, adding that development will strengthen India’s AI infrastructure while supporting growing global demand for advanced compute.
 
 
The integrated AI factory will bring together hyperscale data center infrastructure, accelerated computing, high-performance networking, ultra-low-latency interconnects, high-throughput parallel storage and comprehensive AI infrastructure operations to enable efficient deployment of demanding AI workload.
 
The company said the factory, being developed at Vyoma.AI's Chennai campus, is envisioned as a gigawatt-scale AI infrastructure hub. Its first phase is designed for 250 MW, supported by 150 MVA of power infrastructure readiness, providing a foundation for future capacity expansion.
 
L&T Chairman and Managing Director SN Subrahmanyan said, “This additional GPU deployment marks another significant milestone in L&T’s vision to build world-class AI infrastructure in India. Our Chennai AI Factory will deliver the scale, performance and resilience required to accelerate global AI innovation and strengthen India’s position as a leading hub for next-generation computing.”
